title: Build macOS and Linux binaries from release tags
objective: Implement tag-triggered versioned macOS/Linux builds with optional signing and automatic GitHub pre-release publication.
context_summary: Owner requests implementation. Short v0.1 normalizes to 0.1.0. The owner explicitly chose automatic GitHub pre-release publication after successful builds and asset uploads. Hosted credentials are a separate operator input from the local luxforge-notarization Keychain profile. Existing broad v0.1 distribution qualification remains open. Reviewed relevant current origin/main changes; no conflicting packaging/version implementation exists. Routine archive and workflow details are delegated. The owner requests a single release command with clean-state/main checks. Add an annotated-tag push only after fresh remote identity and local quick checks; dry-run is read-only and skips quick checks. Re-reviewed current origin/main; its unrelated grading/CI changes do not conflict with this command.

tasks.description: Add the guarded release TAG command, isolated Git failure tests and operator instructions.
extra_context: Implement the release command contract in docs/design/tag-release-builds.md. The owner requests tooling, not a real release invocation or credential upload.
Use the existing tag parser and lightweight xtask route. Routine Git command organization and fixture mechanics are delegated; do not add a generalized deployment service.

context_links.label: Release command contract
context_links.relevance: Checks, dry-run, mutation order and failure behavior

acceptance_criteria: Invalid tag, dirty/staged/untracked state, detached or non-main branch, missing workflow/origin, unsynchronized remote main and existing normalized local/remote versions fail before creating or pushing a tag.
Successful quick checks are followed by fresh state checks; an annotated tag names the verified commit and only that tag reaches the configured push destination.
Dry-run mutates nothing and skips quick checks; failed checks create no tag; failed push retains the local tag and reports recovery without overwriting remote tags.
Focused isolated Git tests and final quick verification pass; no actual owner-remote release is triggered.

steps: Exercise clean main and each rejection using temporary repositories and local bare remotes; inject check failure/state changes and reject a push. Verify lightweight command routing and docs.
expected_results: Preflight failures and dry-run preserve refs, success pushes one annotated tag, state changes stop release, rejected push retains its local tag, and quick verification passes.
